phonemes.description: A voiceless stop made with both lips, with a puff of air at the start of a word.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Press your lips together, build up air, then release it in a quick burst with no voicing.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Please put the paper in the proper place.

phonemes.description: A voiced stop made with both lips, like a softer version of 'p'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Press your lips together and release while keeping your voice on, with little or no puff of air.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The big brown bear bumped the table.

phonemes.description: A voiceless stop made by tapping the tongue tip behind the upper teeth, with a puff of air.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Touch the ridge behind your top teeth with your tongue tip, hold the air, then release it sharply without voicing.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Take time to talk to the teacher.

phonemes.description: A voiced stop made just behind the upper teeth, the voiced partner of 't'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Place your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth and release while voicing, with little air.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Dad decided to do the dishes today.

phonemes.description: A voiceless stop made at the back of the mouth, with a puff of air at the start of a word.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate, block the air, then release it with no voicing.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Keep the cards in the kitchen cabinet.

phonemes.description: A voiced stop made at the back of the mouth, the voiced partner of 'k'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate and release while keeping your voice on.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The good dog got a green bag.

phonemes.description: A voiceless affricate that begins like 't' and ends in a 'sh' rush of air.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Stop the air with your tongue on the ridge, then release it into a 'sh' sound, all without voicing.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Each child chose a cheese sandwich.

phonemes.description: A voiced affricate that begins like 'd' and ends in a 'zh' buzz, the voiced partner of 'ch'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Stop the air with your tongue on the ridge, then release it into a buzzing 'zh' while voicing.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Just enjoy the orange juice and jam.

phonemes.description: A voiceless fricative made by pushing air between the top teeth and lower lip.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Rest your top teeth lightly on your lower lip and blow air through without voicing.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Find five fresh figs for the family.

phonemes.description: A voiced fricative made between the top teeth and lower lip, the voiced partner of 'f'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Rest your top teeth lightly on your lower lip and blow air while keeping your voice on.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Victor loves visiting the village.

phonemes.description: A voiceless fricative made with the tongue tip between the teeth (the 'th' in 'think').
phonemes.howToArticulate: Stick your tongue tip lightly between your teeth and blow air through without voicing.
phonemes.practiceSentence: I think the thin path is the third one.

phonemes.description: A voiced fricative made with the tongue between the teeth (the 'th' in 'this').
phonemes.howToArticulate: Place your tongue tip lightly between your teeth and let your voice buzz as air passes.
phonemes.practiceSentence: They gathered there with their mother.

phonemes.description: A voiceless fricative made by hissing air over the tongue behind the teeth.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Raise the front of your tongue near the ridge behind your teeth and push a thin stream of air through.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Sam sees seven small stars.

phonemes.description: A voiced fricative, the buzzing partner of 's'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Make the same shape as 's' but turn on your voice so the air buzzes.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The lazy bees buzz in the zoo.

phonemes.description: A voiceless fricative made with a 'shh' sound, tongue pulled slightly back.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Round your lips a little, pull your tongue back from the 's' position, and push air to make 'shh'.
phonemes.practiceSentence: She should wash the shiny shells.

phonemes.description: A voiced fricative, the buzzing 'zh' partner of 'sh'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Make the 'sh' shape but turn on your voice so the air buzzes, as in 'measure'.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The treasure gave us great pleasure.

phonemes.description: A voiceless breathy sound made by pushing air out of an open mouth.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Open your mouth and breathe out gently, as if fogging a mirror, with no other constriction.
phonemes.practiceSentence: He has a happy and healthy habit.

phonemes.description: A voiced nasal made by humming with both lips closed.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Close your lips and let your voice come out through your nose.
phonemes.practiceSentence: My mom made a small meal.

phonemes.description: A voiced nasal made with the tongue tip behind the upper teeth.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Touch the ridge behind your top teeth with your tongue tip and let your voice flow out your nose.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Nine new nurses need names.

phonemes.description: A voiced nasal made at the back of the mouth (the 'ng' in 'sing').
phonemes.howToArticulate: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate, like for 'g', but send your voice through your nose.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The singer was bringing strong songs.

phonemes.description: A voiced sound made by touching the tongue tip behind the teeth and letting air flow around the sides.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Touch the ridge behind your top teeth with your tongue tip and let your voice flow over the sides of your tongue.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Lily likes the little yellow ball.

phonemes.description: The voiced American 'r', made without the tongue touching anything.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Curl or bunch your tongue back without touching the roof of your mouth, round your lips slightly, and voice it.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Robert read a really great story.

phonemes.description: A voiced glide made with rounded lips that slides into the next vowel.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Round your lips tightly as for 'oo', then quickly open into the following vowel while voicing.
phonemes.practiceSentence: We will wait for the warm weather.

phonemes.description: A voiced glide that starts near 'ee' and slides into the next vowel (the 'y' in 'yes').
phonemes.howToArticulate: Raise the front of your tongue toward the roof as for 'ee', then glide into the following vowel.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Yesterday you used your yellow yo-yo.

phonemes.description: A long, tense front vowel with spread lips, as in 'see'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Smile slightly and raise the front of your tongue high, holding the sound long and steady.
phonemes.practiceSentence: She sees the green trees by the sea.

phonemes.description: A short, relaxed front vowel, looser and lower than 'ee', as in 'sit'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Relax your tongue just below the 'ee' position and keep the sound short and lax.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Tim will fix the big ship.

phonemes.description: A short mid-front vowel, mouth a little more open than 'ih', as in 'bed'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Drop your jaw a bit from the 'ih' position and keep your tongue in the front of your mouth.
phonemes.practiceSentence: Ten men went to the red tent.

phonemes.description: A short, open front vowel with the mouth wide, as in 'cat'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Open your mouth wide, keep your tongue low and forward, and let the sound be flat and bright.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The cat sat on the black mat.

phonemes.description: A short, central vowel with a relaxed, open mouth, as in 'cup'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Keep your tongue in a neutral, central position and your mouth slightly open, with a short relaxed sound.
phonemes.practiceSentence: My uncle won the running cup.

phonemes.description: A long, open back vowel with the mouth wide, as in 'father'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Open your mouth wide, drop your tongue low and toward the back, and hold the sound long.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The calm father parked the car far away.

phonemes.description: A long, rounded back vowel, as in 'thought' or 'law'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Round your lips, raise the back of your tongue a little, and hold the sound long.
phonemes.practiceSentence: I bought a tall ball at dawn.

phonemes.description: A short, relaxed rounded back vowel, as in 'book'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Round your lips loosely and raise the back of your tongue partway, keeping the sound short and lax.
phonemes.practiceSentence: She took a good look at the book.

phonemes.description: A long, tense rounded back vowel, as in 'blue' or 'food'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Round your lips tightly, raise the back of your tongue high, and hold the sound long and steady.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The blue moon shone over the pool.

phonemes.description: The schwa: a short, weak, neutral vowel used in unstressed syllables, as in 'about'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Relax your tongue and lips completely in the center of your mouth and make a very short, soft sound.
phonemes.practiceSentence: A banana and a sofa are common around here.

phonemes.description: An r-colored schwa: the unstressed 'er' at the end of words like 'teacher'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Make a relaxed central schwa while curling or bunching your tongue back for an 'r' color.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The teacher gave the doctor better water.

phonemes.description: A long, stressed r-colored central vowel, as in 'bird' or 'her'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Hold a central vowel long while curling or bunching your tongue back for a strong 'r' color.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The early bird heard the first word.

phonemes.description: A diphthong that glides from a mid-front vowel up toward 'ee', as in 'say'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Start with a relaxed 'eh', then glide smoothly up and forward toward 'ee' in one motion.
phonemes.practiceSentence: They came to play on the same day.

phonemes.description: A diphthong that glides from an open vowel up toward 'ee', as in 'my'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Start with an open 'ah', then glide smoothly up toward 'ee' in one continuous motion.
phonemes.practiceSentence: I tried to find my bright kite.

phonemes.description: A diphthong that glides from a rounded back vowel up toward 'ee', as in 'boy'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Start with a rounded 'aw', then glide forward and up toward 'ee' in one motion.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The boy enjoyed his new toy.

phonemes.description: A diphthong that glides from an open vowel toward 'oo', as in 'now'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Start with an open 'ah', then glide back and round your lips toward 'oo' in one motion.
phonemes.practiceSentence: The brown cow is out in the town now.

phonemes.description: A diphthong that glides from a mid-back vowel toward 'oo', as in 'go'.
phonemes.howToArticulate: Start with a rounded 'oh', then glide up and round further toward 'oo' in one smooth motion.
phonemes.practiceSentence: I know we won't go home alone.
